item.description: Nate Eaton Trade Details: Red Sox Acquire Pitcher in Deal With Athletics originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Boston Red Sox have made their first trade of the offseason, sending outfielder Nate Eaton to the Athletics in exchange for right-handed pitching prospect Jareth Rayo. The #RedSox today traded OF Nate Eaton to the Athletics, in exchange for minor league RHP Jareth Rayo. — Red Sox (@RedSox) October 29, 2026 USA Today's Bob Nightengale first reported the Eaton trade, while Francys Romero reported that Boston would receive Rayo in return. The deal gives the Red Sox another young arm to develop as they begin shaping their roster for the 2027 season. Rayo, 18, spent his first professional season in the Dominican Summer League after joining the Athletics organization as an international amateur. The Nicaragua native stands 6-foot-3 and weighs 195 pounds. The right-hander made 11 appearances, including nine starts, in 2026. He finished with a 1-1 record and a 5.50 ERA across 36 innings, striking out 36 batters while issuing 20 walks. Those numbers offer an early look at Rayo's potential and the areas he must refine as he advances through professional baseball. He has yet to pitch above rookie ball, making him a developmental addition rather than an immediate option for Boston's major-league staff. Nate Eaton's Time With the Red Sox Eaton spent the 2026 season moving between Boston and Triple-A Worcester, serving as a depth option for a club navigating a long major-league schedule. The 29-year-old appeared in 24 regular-season games with the Red Sox, batting .160 with one home run and six RBIs across 50 at-bats. He also appeared in the American League Wild Card Series against the New York Yankees, going 1-for-2. His production was stronger at Worcester . Eaton played 84 games with the WooSox, hitting .253 with a .338 on-base percentage and a .410 slugging percentage. He added nine home runs, 44 RBIs and 18 stolen bases, providing a combination of power and speed at the Triple-A level. Eaton's defensive versatility was another part of his value. He could provide coverage in the outfield and at third base, giving Boston flexibility when making lineup changes or managing its bench. The Kansas City Royals selected Eaton in the 21st round of the 2018 MLB Draft out of Virginia Military Institute. He made his major-league debut in 2022 and later joined Boston, appearing in games for the Red Sox during the 2025 and 2026 seasons. His limited opportunities at the plate in 2026 made it difficult to establish himself as a regular contributor in Boston. The trade gives him a fresh opportunity with the Athletics as he looks to earn a more consistent place in a major-league organization. item.title: June Jones dies at 73: Run-and-shoot innovator changed Hawaii football forever
item.description: June Jones, former Hawaiʻi and SMU football coach who was behind the Rainbow Warriors ' perfect regular season in 2007, died at age 73. His Run and Shoot Certification coaching program announced Jones' death Thursday, Oct. 29. "June’s greatest legacy wasn’t the records, championships, or the offense. It was the people he believed in, the opportunities he gave, and the lives he forever changed," it said on social media . More: Hawaiʻi traveled 4,255 miles for college football’s strangest conference game Jones was a quarterback for Oregon, Hawaiʻi and Portland State, where he learned the run-and-shoot offense that focused heavily on passing. He was an assistant at the professional level until he got his first head coaching job with Hawaiʻi in 1999. He brought the run-and-shoot offense to the Rainbow Warriors and turned them into an exciting team that was annually among the best passing units in the country, including quarterback Timmy Chang becoming the all-time NCAA leader in passing yardage. His best season came in 2007, where behind Heisman Trophy finalist Colt Brennan, Hawaiʻi went 12-0 for the first undefeated regular season in school history, captivating the islands and filling up Aloha Stadium. Hawaiʻi appeared in its first BCS Bowl game in the Sugar Bowl, losing to Georgia 41-10. After the record season, Jones coached at SMU from 2008-14, leading the Mustangs to four bowl games during his tenure. He then spent time coaching at various levels of football, from the Canadian Football League to the XFL. As a college football coach, Jones went 112–84 with two conference titles at Hawaiʻi and the winningest coach in Rainbow Warriors football history with 76 wins. item.title: Colts’ Jonathan Taylor Gets Honest Amid Swirling Trade Rumors
item.description: The Indianapolis Colts have officially started their fire sale before the upcoming NFL trade deadline on November 10. So far this week, the Colts have pulled off two trades. Those deals sent star offensive line Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks and star defensive tackle DeForest Buckner back to the San Francisco 49ers. Nelson was acquired by the Seahawks in exchange for a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round selection. As for Bucker, the 49ers only had to give up a 2027 fourth-round pick to get him. While the two moves were blockbuster deals, it doesn’t seem likely that Indianapolis is done. Josh Downs, Grover Stewart, and Jonathan Taylor have all come up as possible trade candidates. Of course, Taylor is the big name out of that group. Whether or not the Colts will actually move Taylor remains to be seen. However, the star running back has spoken out honestly with his thoughts as the rumors persist. Oct 17, 2021; Indianapolis, Indiana, USA; Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor (28) runs the ball while Houston Texans cornerback Terrance Mitchell (39) defends in the second half at Lucas Oil Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Trevor Ruszkowski-USA TODAY Sports Colts Star Jonathan Taylor Speaks Out About Trade Rumors As shared by Mike Chappel of Fox 59 in Indianapolis, Taylor is focusing on football rather than the rumors. He still seems to love playing for the Colts. “I haven’t heard anything, and I can’t control that,” Taylor said . “Obviously, I’m always proud to wear the horseshoe and proud to be here. Similar to Quenton and Buck, they were proud to wear the horseshoe and proud to be here. But circumstances may cause otherwise. Hopefully, that day doesn’t come, but I can’t control that.” Taylor has been the workhorse for the Indianapolis offense in recent years. He is one of the best running backs in the NFL. Keeping him around would be ideal for the Colts, but they could acquire good draft capital if they chose to move him. So far this season in seven games played, Taylor has carried the football 140 times for 587 yards and eight touchdowns. He has also caught 17 passes for 178 yards. Last season, the superstar running back put up massive numbers. He racked up 1,585 yards and 18 touchdowns on 323 carries, while also catching 46 passes for 378 yards and two more scores. Expect to continue hearing rumors about Taylor as the trade deadline draws closer. For now, he is simply focused on playing for the Colts and is not paying attention to the outside noise. item.title: You Won’t Believe How Much Money Brewers Players Take Home for Winning the World Series
item.description: AARON JOSEFCZYK/UPI/Newscom/The Mega Agency The Milwaukee Brewers ‘ first World Series title in their 56 years in Wisconsin wasn’t the only prize they took home on Wednesday, October 28. The championship also comes with a sizable postseason payout for the team to split. Under MLB ‘s definition of postseason share , the pool is funded by gate receipts from the 12 teams that reach the playoffs. It draws 50 percent of the gate from the Wild Card Games, 60 percent from the first three games of the Division Series, and 60 percent from the first four games of both the League Championship Series and the World Series. AARON JOSEFCZYK/UPI/Newscom/The Mega Agency How that money gets divided depends on how far each team goes. According to The Sporting Page , the World Series champion receives 36 percent of the pool, and the runner-up gets 24 percent. The rest is split among the other playoff teams based on how far they advanced. Based on past pool totals, a World Series winner typically has millions of dollars to distribute. The players themselves vote on how much to give to non-players such as coaches, trainers and other club personnel. That means the money reaches many people throughout the organization, not just those on the field. AARON JOSEFCZYK/UPI/Newscom/The Mega Agency MLB hasn’t released the total for the 2026 postseason yet. It publishes the numbers every year, though, so last season gives us a good idea of what the Brewers could take home: The Los Angeles Dodgers won the 2025 World Series, and their postseason pool totaled $128.2 million. That meant each full share came to $484,747.57. Barcelona board make feelings clear about Hansi Flick and players after consecutive defeats
item.description: Barcelona board make feelings clear about Hansi Flick and players after consecutive defeats Barcelona’s impressive start to the season suffered an unexpected setback following consecutive defeats against PSG and Real Madrid. The results have exposed weaknesses in Hansi Flick’s team. However, the club’s leadership is not losing faith in the project. According to journalist Achraf Ben Ayad , Barcelona’s board expressed complete confidence in the players and coaching staff during its latest meeting. Despite the disappointing results, the decision-makers remain firmly behind the German manager and believe the squad can recover its best form. Barcelona board maintains complete faith in Flick Sunday’s 2-1 Clasico defeat to Real Madrid saw Barcelona’s advantage in La Liga reduced to just three points. The Catalans had won their opening nine league matches, scoring goals for fun and looking unstoppable. The board retain complete faith in Barcelona’s project. (Photo by Eric Alonso/Getty Images) However, they ran into a resolute Real Madrid side at the Spotify Camp Nou who came with a clear plan and played Barcelona off the park. Club president Joan Laporta had already defended Flick following the Clasico , insisting: “It was a tough blow, but the players are young and they bounce back quickly. We weren’t able to play our usual game, but we’re still top of the table. “We’re still top of La Liga and our expectations remain intact. And Flick is the ideal manager for Barça.” Barcelona determined to respond after difficult week Interestingly, the board’s backing follows a separate initiative within the dressing room, where Raphinha and Rodri helped organise a team barbecue on Wednesday to strengthen unity. The players are said to have discussed their recent mistakes at that gathering, including poor pressing, careless passing and insufficient defensive cover. They have, however, maintained that they can return to their best level if they iron out the issues that have crept into their game. Two losses don’t take away the start Barcelona have had to the season. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) Flick has done an excellent job of assembling this squad and getting them to play a recognisable style of football. The two defeats in the last week should not overshadow the fact that this remains an excellent start to the season for Barcelona, who have won 11 of their first 13 games. The Catalans now face Alaves, Aston Villa and Atletico Madrid before the international break, giving the squad a chance to bounce back. The board has also made their position on Flick clear, and it never really seemed to be in doubt. It remains to be seen whether the team have learnt from their errors and can put on a show against Alaves this weekend.

item.title: FC Cincinnati announces 2027 Sprint Season MLS schedule
item.description: Major League Soccer has announced FC Cincinnati’s full schedule for the 2027 MLS Sprint Season. The 2027 MLS Sprint Season will launch the league’s transition into its new summer-to-spring calendar and aligns its schedule with the world’s top soccer leagues. The season will begin the weekend of February 19-21 and culminate in the Audi 2027 MLS Cup Playoffs and 2027 MLS Cup on Memorial Day Weekend in May. Cincinnati will start the season in the place they just left, Miami’s Nu Stadium. Cincinnati will play Inter Miami CF Friday, Feb. 19 at 8 p.m., which will be the opening game for the entire league. The Orange and Blue’s home opener comes eight days later on Saturday, February 27 in a 3 p.m. ET kickoff at TQL Stadium against New York City FC. The regular season will be 14 games, all in the same conference. Cincinnati will play seven home games against Eastern Conference foes, and seven away. FC Cincinnati will additionally host Orlando City SC (March 6), 2026 Supporters’ Shield-winners Nashville SC (March 20), Chicago Fire FC (April 7), New England Revolution (April 10), Toronto FC (April 21) and, in the club’s home finale, the Columbus Crew on April 24 in the lone regular season Hell is Real derby of the 2027 Sprint Season. Road trips following the season opener in South Florida include away matches at Charlotte FC (March 3), D.C. United (March 13), Red Bull New York (March 27), Philadelphia Union (April 3), Atlanta United FC (April 17) and Decision Day north of the border at CF Montréal on May 8. Sprint Season single-match tickets are on sale now for 2026 FC Cincinnati Season Ticket Members, Orange and Blue Reserve Members, and Ticket Pack purchasers. Tickets go on sale to the general public Friday, October 30 at 10 a.m. ET at FCCincinnati.com/Tickets or by calling 513-977-KICK. The playoffs will be tweaked from the current format. Eight teams from each conference will make the playoffs, and each round is a single-elimination game. The available trophies will remain the same, with the league awarding a Supporters’ Shield champion and MLS Cup champion. Teams can also win berths in the 2028 Concacaf Champions Cup and Leagues Cup. Following the end of the Sprint Season, the full 2027-28 season will begin sometime in July. item.title: As 2027 MLS Schedule Released, These 5 Things Stand Out
item.description: CINCINNATI, OHIO - NOVEMBER 23: Lionel Messi #10 of Inter Miami CF greets players of FC Cincinnati prior to the Conference Semifinal match between FC Cincinnati and Inter Miami FC as part of the 2025 MLS Cup Playoffs at TQL Stadium on November 23, 2025 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Jeff Dean/Getty Images) Getty Images Major League Soccer released the schedule for its 2027 sprint season on Thursday, giving fans more details on just what a unique four months in the league’s history will look like. The league is playing a condensed, 14-match regular season plus playoffs from the middle of February to the end of May to enable the calendar flip coming in later 2027 . The full MLS regular season will return in late July and be contested in a summer-to-spring format similar to the Premier League, La Liga and other top soccer competitions. The 2027 sprint season will provide teams a second chance to win an MLS Cup in about six months. And it features some interesting tweaks to what we’re used to. A Slightly Earlier Start Arguably the most interesting detail involves kickoff times. According to early information on MLS’ website, the league’s announced kickoff times will now be overwhelmingly on the top of a given hour. For night matches, this typically means a 7 p.m. ET kickoff rather than 7:30 p.m. ET. Cold Weather Leniency As MLS prepares for its schedule switch, it seems like allowing colder markets to schedule more daytime matches will become the norm. The five coldest markets in the league -- Montreal, Toronto, New England, Minnesota and Chicago -- will combine to play 13 true home matches in late February and March. Only one will kick off after 5 p.m. local time: Chicago’s tilt against Atlanta United set for 8 p.m. ET on March 27. CF Montreal Heads to Florida Meanwhile, with renovations at Stade Olimpique in Montreal still ongoing , MLS will no longer allow the French Canadian club to start its season with six or more consecutive away matches. This time Montreal’s first home game will come on Matchday 3, sort of. Technically they’ll be the home team against D.C. United, but the match will be played at Inter Miami’s Nu Stadium on March 7. Super Bowl Sequel The opening match between Inter Miami and FC Cincinnati on Feb. 19 and the rest of opening weekend on Feb. 20-21 represent the earliest start to an MLS season in the league’s history, but only marginally. In 2026, competition began on Feb. 21-22, in 2025 on Feb. 22-23 and so on. It’s also the first weekend after the NFL stages Super Bowl XLI on Feb. 14. In the future, MLS will take a winter break starting sometime in December and ending sometime in February. Perhaps this suggests the league remains wary of moving its start date ahead of the NFL finale. Condensed Playoffs The sprint season concludes with a 16-team, single-elimination playoff structure that will be played following the final day of the regular season on May 8 and conclude before the end of the month. item.description: ‘We have to back this up’ – Arsenal must keep building says Slegers Arsenal head coach Renée Slegers says that her side need to keep building on their recent upturn in results. The Gunners won just two of their first eight matches this season, but they have since recorded back-to-back victories in the past week. When speaking to the media ahead of this weekend’s Barclays Women’s Super League fixture against Aston Villa, Slegers said that recent results have lifted the mood, but it is important to keep building. “Of course, it’s lighter [after two wins],” Slegers said. “You work so hard for the rewards and we are here to win. We’ve done that twice now, which is great, but we have to back this up as well. We said it after Spurs in the North London derby and it’s the exact same now. It’s good, it’s two good wins. It was Arsenal, this was us last night and now, we have to back it up with the next game coming up against Villa.” Latest opponents Aston Villa are in good form and Slegers is looking forward to the test that will be provided by the Midlands side. She said “With Brian [Sørensen], they’ve had a really good start; I think it’s four wins and a draw. They won last night through penalties. “We remember the game last year, how it was difficult at Emirates for us at home. The away game was good, it was dominant. We have to be prepared, we have to be humble. “What they’re going to do, it’s always a guessing game. Of course, they’re in a transition now and they’ve changed their system. Let’s see what they do against us. Very often it happens that teams do something different against us. Let’s see what their game plan is. We have to focus on ourselves and keep building on our last performance.” Four of Arsenal’s next six games are on home soil and Slegers is looking forward to many opportunities to play in-front of the club’s fans. item.title: Scottish football could pave way for 3pm TV blackout to end
item.description: Games currently cannot be shown live between 2:45pm and 5:15pm on a Saturday [Getty Images] The first tentative steps to end the 3pm television blackout have been taken by Scottish football as it seeks offers for the next broadcast cycle. The SPFL has said that it is "flexible about the number of games" that will form part of the new deal, which will kick in from the 2029-30 season. BBC Sport understands this includes the possibility that broadcasters could bid to show all matches live - including those shown on a Saturday afternoon. The SPFL has created a tender with the greatest flexibility on the basis that the broadcaster does not seek to impose Article 48 of the Uefa Statutes. Article 48 allows leagues to set specific times when matches are banned from being shown live on television. It can only be enforced when 50% of matches in a country's top two divisions are played at the same time. While other parts of Europe have experimented with a blackout, it is now only present in the UK between 2:45pm and 5:15pm on a Saturday. Other leagues now tend to stagger kick-off times so the top divisions do not all play at the same time, meaning the blackout could not be applied. In the UK, 3pm remains the traditional, default kick-off time for all leagues from the very top down through non-league. It was introduced due to fears that televised games at 3pm could affect attendances, not just at the clubs involved but at those down the divisions too. But as streaming has grown in popularity, critics have argued that it hinders the ability of clubs to exploit this revenue stream. This is especially the case in the lower levels, which have had to adhere to the blackout and not show any of their games online. The Cymru Premier, the top division of football in Wales which has a mixture of professional and semi-professional clubs, removed the blackout in the summer in favour of a streaming model for all matches. In August, Premier League chief executive Richard Masters indicated the direction of travel was to end the blackout, but any decision would be 18 months away and taken in consultation with the EFL and the FA. The upcoming broadcast cycle provides a unique opportunity for all leagues to come together and reach a consensus, as the rights deals for the Premier League, EFL and SPFL all end in 2028-29. While the possibility to take all games is on the table in Scotland, it is by no means certain the option will be taken up. Under the current terms, Sky Sports can show up to 60 Premiership matches a season, with Premier Sports showing up to 22. In total, there are 228 games in the top flight, meaning only 36% of matches are shown live under the current broadcast deal. The tender allows broadcasters to present any proposition for live coverage they see fit. Any decision would then be up to the Premiership's 12 member clubs, with eight votes required to approve a deal. item.title: Lake View volleyball's long climb ends with a return to the postseason
item.description: On a Saturday in early September 2025, the Lake View volleyball team won a district match against Big Spring 25-21, 25-23, 25-20. It was the first district win for new coach Kaylee Morgan with the Maidens. What looked like an innocuous district matchup, was a massive step forward for Lake View. After winning a share of the district title in 2022, the Maidens had two seasons without a district win and had one total victory between 2023-24. Now, in Morgan’s second year at the helm, Lake View is headed back to the postseason after finishing 14-15 overall and 5-7 in district play. More: West Texas, San Angelo high school volleyball bi-district schedule and scores More: Morales punches ticket to state cross country meet For Morgan, the turnaround had been a rewarding experience built on belief, accountability and a shared commitment from her players. “It feels beyond amazing,” Morgan said. “I am super proud of what the girls have been able to accomplish this year.” The rebuilding process began last season when Lake View improved to 7-20 overall and 3-7 in district. Those early victories helped lay the foundation for a bigger breakthrough this fall. "We talked about the goals that we had as a team at the beginning of the year," Morgan said. "Everyone wanted to be on the same level with everything. Whether that was how hard we fought, how hard we practiced or how competitive we were, the girls really wanted to succeed." Among those goals were winning more matches, improving their district record, bringing home tournament hardware and earning a playoff berth. Morgan said the team’s confidence growing tournament play at the Bev Ball and Nita Vannoy tournaments. Particularly, with their performance at the West Texas Fest in Sonora. "That was really a point for me where I thought, 'They've got this. They can do it,'" Morgan said. "The improvement and them coming together as a team really stood out." Many of the players who fought through the years where there were less wins, Morgan said helped drive the resurgence. She highlighted senior middle hitter Soraya Morrison for her energy and competitiveness, junior outside hitter Lexi Martinez for her focus and Livia Garcia for her relentless hustle. The team’s confidence growth came to a head when they faced-off against Levelland on the road with a playoff berth on the line. "It was a very heartfelt moment as a coach to see them so happy and confident in what they were able to accomplish," Morgan said after Lake View rallied to win three straight sets against Levelland to clinch a playoff berth. "There were some tears, but I was glad the girls got to experience that moment." The Maidens' success has brought even more support from the Lake View community. "Our parents, our community, the fans, the staff, everyone, to see them in the stands a little bit more and hear how proud they are of the girls, that's been huge," Morgan said.
